That monthly rate is a 214% year: MoM and YoY are the same number wearing different clothes.

Reaching the target49 months

At today's rate you hit ₹1Cr a month in 49 months.

MoM is how much this month beat last month. YoY compares against the same period a year earlier. They're the same growth seen at two speeds: 10.0% a month compounds to 214% across twelve.

Year 5 at this trajectory

Holding 50% YoY after year one puts year 5 at ₹1.08Cr and ₹8.66L of net profit at a 8.0% margin. The whole path traces back to the monthly rate, which is why one point matters more than it looks.

Questions this calculator answers

How do you convert MoM growth to YoY growth?

Compound the monthly rate over twelve months: YoY = (1 + MoM)^12 − 1. A steady 10% month-on-month compounds to roughly 214% year-on-year, which is why small monthly gains matter far more than they appear.

What is a good MoM growth rate for a D2C brand?

It depends entirely on the base. Early brands at a low run rate can post 15–20% MoM for a while; at scale, sustained 5–8% MoM is strong. Any MoM figure quoted without the starting revenue is close to meaningless.

How many months does it take to double revenue?

Divide the natural log of 2 by the natural log of one plus your monthly growth rate. At 10% MoM it takes about 7.3 months; at 5% MoM it takes roughly 14.2 months.
